summary: Roger Blanchard, a chemistry teacher and author of a book on global oil production, argues that world oil supply is finite and that current consumption is unsustainable, contrary to the optimistic outlook he attributes to mainstream media and the US EIA. He cites production, discovery and consumption figures, the steep decline of shale wells outside sweet spots, the decline of major fields such as Cantarell and Prudhoe Bay, and his view that the Permian Basin, ANWR and NPRA offer limited future gains. The page's comment section is cut off, and the navigation, share buttons and related-article boilerplate were ignored.
one_line: Roger Blanchard argues that finite oil supply is being depleted fast, that EIA forecasts are overly optimistic, and that shale and Arctic oil will not last.
key_facts: Global crude oil plus condensate production in 2017 was about 30 billion barrels.
Cumulative world oil production at the end of 2017 was approximately 1.36 trillion barrels.
Jean Laherrere estimated ultimate recoverable oil, excluding extra heavy oil, at approximately 2.2 trillion barrels in 2013.
The author expects economically recoverable oil to be less than 3 trillion barrels.
In recent years the rate of global oil discovery has been running less than 1/5th the rate of global oil consumption.
Global oil consumption rose nearly 1 million barrels/day per year on average from 2000 to 2017.
The EIA predicted global petroleum consumption would increase about 1.6 mb/d in 2018.
The energy per unit mass of lithium ion batteries used in electric vehicles is less than 1/50th that of gasoline or diesel fuel.
The federal government provides a $7,500 tax credit for electric vehicle purchases.
From 2010 to 2015, U.S. light tight oil production increased by 3.933 mb/d and Iraq production rose from 2.398 mb/d to 4.050 mb/d.
About 90% of Bakken oil production in North Dakota comes from 4 of the 16 counties in the Bakken region.
For 2008-2017, total Bakken Shale oil production in North Dakota was 2.32 billion barrels, versus an estimated economically recoverable 5 billion barrels.
Production from fracked wells generally declines by 70-90% by the end of the 3rd year of production.
Since 2012, natural gas production from the Barnett Shale has declined by over 40%.
The Cantarell Complex in Mexico produced 2.1 mb/d in 2004 and about 0.25 mb/d presently, roughly 12% of maximum production.
Prudhoe Bay with its satellite fields produced about 0.28 mb/d in 2017, which is 17.5% of maximum production.
